channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Cross-Validation Folds for Grouped Data: Silent Leakage
item.description: Random folds leak when data has groups: patients, users, sessions. Here's why the fix is grouped splitting, not more data.

item.title: What a Machine Learning Engineer's Week Actually Looks Like
item.description: The job is less 'train a model' and more data cleaning, evaluation design, and stopping silent failures before they reach production.

item.title: NLP Techniques Before Deep Learning: A Practical Refresher
item.description: Classic NLP methods still catch leakage, expose weak baselines and explain model behaviour better than most deep nets ever will.

item.title: Designing an Evaluation Harness Before You Know the Job
item.description: A practical guide to building leakage-aware, adaptable evaluation harnesses for models whose final job is not yet fully defined.

item.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks: What Red-Teaming Tests
item.description: Red-teaming finds failures; it does not bound risk. Here is what it actually measures, with a worked example showing why absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

item.title: The Transformer Architecture, Explained Without the Maths
item.description: A no-equations tour of transformers: what attention actually does, why position matters, and why the architecture scaled so well.

item.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: What Actually Gets Updated
item.description: A worked look at how adapters and LoRA fine-tune large models by updating a small slice of parameters, and why that matters for real projects.

item.title: The Cost Matrix Nobody Writes Down
item.description: Most models are trained to minimise a generic loss while the business quietly cares about wildly asymmetric costs. Here is how to fix that mismatch.

item.title: SHAP, LIME, and When Neither Method Is Honest
item.description: SHAP and LIME answer different questions dressed up as the same question. Knowing the difference is the line between insight and false confidence.

item.title: When Is a Model Good Enough to Ship? Beyond Accuracy
item.description: Accuracy alone can't tell you if a model is safe to deploy. Here's how to set real thresholds around cost, calibration, and failure modes before you ship.

item.title: Synthetic Benchmarks vs Real Data: Why Rank Slips
item.description: Topping a leaderboard tells you about the leaderboard. It rarely tells you what happens when your model meets the messy world.

item.title: What a Learning Curve Tells You That Accuracy Cannot
item.description: One accuracy score tells you where you are. A learning curve tells you why, and what to do about it.

item.title: A Worked Example of Bayesian Model Comparison
item.description: A concrete walkthrough of Bayesian model comparison, showing how Bayes factors give a richer answer than a single p-value ever can.

item.title: Time Series Cross-Validation: Why Shuffled Folds Ruin Everything
item.description: Shuffling time series folds lets the future leak into training, inflating validation scores and hiding models that will fail in production.

item.title: Multi-Label vs Multi-Class: Metrics Quietly Misapplied
item.description: Multi-class metrics silently misused on multi-label problems produce numbers that look fine and mean almost nothing.

item.title: Ablation Studies: Isolating What Actually Helped
item.description: A new module, a new loss, a better score: but which change actually mattered? Ablations tell you, if you design them properly.

item.title: Baseline Models You Should Always Try First
item.description: A strong baseline is not a formality, it is the number every fancy model must beat to justify its cost.

item.title: The Stationarity Assumption Hiding Inside Your Metrics
item.description: Accuracy, AUC and their friends all assume tomorrow looks like today. I unpack that assumption and show, with numbers, how quietly it can fail.

item.title: Data Drift Versus Concept Drift: Same Dashboard, Different Fix
item.description: Your model's accuracy dropped and the input distribution shifted too. That doesn't mean the shift caused the drop. Here's how to tell drift types apart.

item.title: Nested Cross-Validation: Why One Loop Isn't Enough
item.description: One CV loop for both tuning and evaluation leaks information. Nested CV separates the two jobs and gives you an honest estimate of generalisation.
